- [InsideEVs / The Autopian: VinFast VF 8 depreciation case study](https://www.theautopian.com/this-vinfast-depreciated-a-whopping-178-per-day-12-for-every-mile-it-was-driven/) — a 2023 VF 8 lost 45.5% of MSRP in 135 days; used 2023 VF 8 Eco at `$13,950` from `$47,200` MSRP (~70% loss in ~3 yrs).

**Other line items:**
- Insurance `$12,240` substituted from Edmunds Volvo EX30 baseline — closest comparable compact BEV SUV; no VinFast-specific data published. May be biased low: VinFast US has a thin parts/repair network (per Autopian write-up).
- Fuel `$2,900` — VF 6 Plus MPGe 85 (page data) vs EX30 117; scaled from EX30 `$2,120` baseline (`$2,120 × 117 / 85 ≈ $2,919`).
- Maintenance `$1,500` — VinFast US warranty: 10yr/125k mi basic, 10yr/unlimited battery (per page data; longer than the 7yr/87k mi figure cited in the task brief). Wear items (tires, brake fluid, cabin filter, wipers) still customer-borne.
- Repairs `$800` — out-of-warranty / non-covered incidents. Estimate uncertain given thin US service network and reported quality issues.
- Financing `$5,700` — scaled from Edmunds EX30 `$7,378` by MSRP ratio (`$7,378 × 36,500 / 47,258`).
- Taxes & fees `$2,920` (~8% of MSRP) — standard estimate.

**Anomaly:** VinFast US is a new market entrant with extreme observed early depreciation on the VF 8 and no comprehensive TCO coverage from the standard sources. These numbers carry materially higher uncertainty than the Volvo trims.
